In April 2014, Nutter signed an executive order largely ending the agreement that allowed the federal government to detain undocumented immigrants arrested in the city prior to release. The only exemption being if the individual is being released following a first or second degree felony conviction and federal officials obtain a warrant from a judge[[37]](#cite_note-37)[[38]](#cite_note-PhillyNutterEndAgreement-38) - effectively making Philadelphia a [sanctuary city](/wiki/Sanctuary_city "Sanctuary city").[[39]](#cite_note-39)[[40]](#cite_note-40) Nutter indicated that the change in policy supports public safety and will help rebuild the trust between police and the immigrant community.[[38]](#cite_note-PhillyNutterEndAgreement-38) The executive order was highlighted in June 2014 after a previously deported undocumented immigrant from [Honduras](/wiki/Honduras "Honduras") was accused of raping a woman in [Rittenhouse Square](/wiki/Rittenhouse_Square "Rittenhouse Square") with the concern that if acquitted, the accused would not be submitted for deportation due to Philadelphia's new policy.[[41]](#cite_note-41)[[42]](#cite_note-42)[[43]](#cite_note-43)

As of 2014, Michael Nutter was a member of Mt. Carmel Baptist Church in [West Philadelphia](/wiki/West_Philadelphia "West Philadelphia").[[44]](#cite_note-uli-44)

In 1984, Mo Yan published his first novella and claim to literary fame, *A Transparent Radish*. The story was originally titled *A Golden Radish*, but was renamed by Xu Huaizhong. Two years later, he published *Red Sorghum* (1986) at *[People's Literature](/wiki/People%27s_Literature "People's Literature")* to great sensation in the literary circles, and attracted [Zhang Yimou](/wiki/Zhang_Yimou "Zhang Yimou") to visit him at the PLA Academy of Art to acquire the adaptation rights for what would become Zhang's directorial debut and win the [Golden Bear](/wiki/Golden_Bear "Golden Bear") at [Berlinale](/wiki/Berlin_International_Film_Festival "Berlin International Film Festival").[[17]](#cite_note-Williford-17)

In 1987, Mo Yan's novella *Joy* was published in the combined first and second issue of *People's Literature*. It fell foul of the ongoing [Anti-Bourgeois Liberalization Campaign](/wiki/Anti-bourgeois_liberalization "Anti-bourgeois liberalization"). The journal's editor-in-chief [Liu Xinwu](/wiki/Liu_Xinwu "Liu Xinwu") was suspended and placed under investigation, and the issue itself was recalled and destroyed.[[18]](#cite_note-:8-18)

In April 1988, Mo Yan published *The Garlic Ballads,* inspired by an incident in Cangshan, Shandong a year ago, when overproduction, collapsing prices, and predatory market administration fees drove farmers to riot outside the county government building. The novel's sympathetic portrayal of an anti-government riot drew no immediate sanction upon publication, but in the aftermath of the [Tiananmen Square crackdown](/wiki/1989_Tiananmen_Square_protests_and_massacre "1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre") of June 1989 it was banned in mainland China and for a period could only be published in Hong Kong and Taiwan; it was unbanned four years later.[[19]](#cite_note-19) The American sinologist [Howard Goldblatt](/wiki/Howard_Goldblatt "Howard Goldblatt"), upon reading the novel, was so struck by it that he resolved to begin translating Mo Yan's work, a decision that would prove instrumental in bringing Mo Yan to international audiences.[[18]](#cite_note-:8-18)

The Vatican City is not a member of the [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") (UN), but the Holy See was granted [observer status](/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly_observers "United Nations General Assembly observers") to the [United Nations General Assembly](/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly") in 1968; the only other country in a similar position is the partially recognized [State of Palestine](/wiki/State_of_Palestine "State of Palestine"). Since it is not a member of the UN, the Vatican City is not subjected to the jurisdiction of the [International Court of Justice](/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice") (ICJ). It engages with UN specialized agencies through its observer status, including the [Central Emergency Response Fund](/wiki/Central_Emergency_Response_Fund "Central Emergency Response Fund"), to which it contributed US$20,000 between 2006 and 2022.[[108]](#cite_note-120)

The Vatican City State is not a member of the [International Criminal Court](/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") (ICC). In Europe, only [Belarus](/wiki/Belarus "Belarus") is also a non-party, non-signatory state. [Ukraine](/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") and [Monaco](/wiki/Monaco "Monaco") are signatory states that have not ratified and [Russia](/wiki/Russia "Russia") withdrew from it in 2016.

The Vatican City State is not a member of the [Council of Europe](/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe") nor a party to the [European Convention on Human Rights](/wiki/European_Convention_on_Human_Rights "European Convention on Human Rights"), thus is not subject to the [European Court of Human Rights](/wiki/European_Court_of_Human_Rights "European Court of Human Rights"). *Minecraft* is a [three-dimensional](/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics") sandbox video game that has no required goals to accomplish, giving players a large amount of freedom in choosing how to play the game.[[6]](#cite_note-IGN_review-17) The game features an optional [achievement](/wiki/Achievement_(video_games) "Achievement (video games)") system.[[7]](#cite_note-18) Gameplay is in the [first-person perspective](/wiki/First-person_(video_games) "First-person (video games)") by default, but players have the option of [third-person perspectives](/wiki/Third-person_(video_games) "Third-person (video games)") (back and front).[[8]](#cite_note-19) The game world is composed of rough 3D objects—mainly cubes, referred to as blocks—representing various materials, such as dirt, stone, ores, [logs](/wiki/Trunk_(botany) "Trunk (botany)"), water, and [lava](/wiki/Lava "Lava"). The core gameplay revolves around picking up and placing these objects. These blocks are arranged in a [voxel](/wiki/Voxel "Voxel") grid, while players can move freely around the world. Players can break, or *mine*, blocks and then place them elsewhere, enabling them to build structures.[[9]](#cite_note-20) Very few blocks are affected by gravity, instead maintaining their voxel position in the air.[[10]](#cite_note-Minecraft_In_Education-21)

Players can craft a wide variety of items, such as armor, which mitigates damage from attacks; weapons (such as [swords](/wiki/Sword "Sword") or [bows and arrows](/wiki/Bows_and_arrows "Bows and arrows")), which allow monsters and animals to be killed more easily; and tools (such as [pickaxes](/wiki/Pickaxe "Pickaxe") or [shovels](/wiki/Shovel "Shovel")), which break certain types of blocks more quickly. [Carlos Sainz Jr.](/wiki/Carlos_Sainz_Jr. "Carlos Sainz Jr.") took seventh place as he started in tenth place after crashing in qualifying. [Fernando Alonso](/wiki/Fernando_Alonso "Fernando Alonso"), [Nico Hülkenberg](/wiki/Nico_H%C3%BClkenberg "Nico Hülkenberg") and [Sergio Pérez](/wiki/Sergio_P%C3%A9rez "Sergio Pérez") rounded off the scoring positions. The Parthenon is an [octastyle](/wiki/Octastyle "Octastyle") [peripteral](/wiki/Peripteral "Peripteral") [Doric](/wiki/Doric_order "Doric order") temple with an [Ionic](/wiki/Ionic_order "Ionic order") [hexastyle](/wiki/Hexastyle "Hexastyle") [amphiprostyle](/wiki/Amphiprostyle "Amphiprostyle") two-chambered [cella](/wiki/Cella "Cella"). The gable-end of the Parthenon features eight columns instead of the traditional six found in typical Doric temples. Although octastyle temples were not entirely unknown, their presence in mainland Doric architecture, along with the wider inner masonry structure, the *[cella](/wiki/Cella "Cella")*,[[64]](#cite_note-64) makes the Parthenon unique in its design.[[note 1]](#cite_note-67) There are seventeen columns on the sides. A ratio of 4:9 proportion is found in the elevation and the relationship of the columns to their spacing (the interaxial). There is a double row of columns at both the front and rear. The *[cella](/wiki/Cella "Cella")* is divided into two compartments. The *[opisthodomos](/wiki/Opisthodomos "Opisthodomos")* (the back room of the cella) contained the monetary contributions of the Delian League. The Redskins gather at the line of scrimmage against the Giants.

The Giants have an old and storied rivalry with the [Washington Commanders](/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders"), dating back to 1932.[[201]](#cite_note-201) While this rivalry is typically given less significance than the rivalries with the Eagles and Cowboys, there have been periods of great competition between the two. In the 1980s the Giants and Redskins, as they were then known, clashed as both struggled against each other for division titles and even Super Bowl Championships. Most notable among these is the 1986 NFC Championship game in which the Giants defeated the Redskins 17–0 to earn their first ever trip to the Super Bowl. Wellington Mara always felt the Redskins were the Giants' oldest and truest rival, and after dying in 2005, the Giants honored their longtime owner by defeating the Redskins 36–0 at home. The Giants lead this series 107–70–4 as of the 2023 season. The Giants' 107 wins against the Washington Commanders are the most wins for one team against one opponent in NFL history.[[202]](#cite_note-202)

German Chancellor [Friedrich Merz](/wiki/Friedrich_Merz "Friedrich Merz"), Macron, British Prime Minister [Keir Starmer](/wiki/Keir_Starmer "Keir Starmer") and Polish Prime Minister [Donald Tusk](/wiki/Donald_Tusk "Donald Tusk") with Ukrainian President [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy") in [Ukraine](/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") in May 2025

In February 2025, Macron characterised Russia as an "existential threat" to Europe, convening a special meeting in Paris to coordinate European responses under the [Weimar+](/wiki/Weimar%2B "Weimar+") framework.[[343]](#cite_note-345) In March 2025, German lawmakers approved an [amendment to the Basic Law](/wiki/German_balanced_budget_amendment "German balanced budget amendment") that would allow [Friedrich Merz](/wiki/Friedrich_Merz "Friedrich Merz")'s government to implement the most massive rearmament of Germany since [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[344]](#cite_note-346) Germany's decision to massively [increase defense spending](/wiki/2020s_European_rearmament "2020s European rearmament") was welcomed by Macron.[[345]](#cite_note-347)

Following the [Israeli strikes on Iran](/wiki/June_2025_Israeli_strikes_on_Iran "June 2025 Israeli strikes on Iran") on 13 June 2025, Macron called for "maximum restraint" while reaffirming "Israel's right to defend itself and ensure its security."[[346]](#cite_note-348) On 17 June 2025, he claimed that president Trump's haste departure from the [G7 summit](/wiki/G7 "G7"), was to reach a cease fire between Israel and Iran. To which Trump responded "Wrong! He has no idea why I am now on my way to Washington, but it certainly has nothing to do with a Cease Fire. Much bigger than that. Whether purposely or not, Emmanuel always gets it wrong. Stay Tuned!".[[347]

Main articles: [OpenAI](/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI") and [xAI (company)](/wiki/XAI_(company) "XAI (company)")

In December 2015, Musk co-founded [OpenAI](/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI"), a [not-for-profit](/wiki/Nonprofit_corporation "Nonprofit corporation") [artificial intelligence](/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") (AI) research company aiming to develop [artificial general intelligence](/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence"), intended to be safe and beneficial to humanity.[[217]](#cite_note-NYT_AI-222) Musk pledged $1 billion of funding to the company,[[218]](#cite_note-223) but only donated $50 million.[[219]](#cite_note-224) In 2018, Musk left the OpenAI board.[[220]](#cite_note-225) Since 2018, OpenAI has made significant advances in machine learning.[[221]](#cite_note-226) In July 2023, Musk launched the artificial intelligence company [xAI](/wiki/XAI_(company) "XAI (company)"), which aims to develop a [generative AI](/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence "Generative artificial intelligence") program that competes with existing offerings like OpenAI's [ChatGPT](/wiki/ChatGPT "ChatGPT"). Musk obtained funding from investors in SpaceX and Tesla,[[222]](#cite_note-227) and xAI hired engineers from Google and OpenAI.[[223]](#cite_note-228)
